body:
`template/.claude/commands/handoff.md.jinja:13` invokes the guard through a `!` pre-execution block whose command carries two bare `$` expansions:

```
!`python3 "$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.claude/hooks/handoff_guard.py" --check "$1"`
```

Claude Code's shell-permission checker refuses to match an allow-rule against a command containing a simple expansion — it cannot know what the expansion resolves to — so the command aborts before anything runs. That is every rendered instance, every id, every interactive leaf.

## Observed

In `pdca-pdca` (rendered from v0.56.0, now on v0.57.0), during a planner session:

```
> /handoff
Error: Shell command permission check failed for pattern
"!`python3 "$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.claude/hooks/handoff_guard.py" --check "$1"`":
Contains simple_expansion
```

The missing argument is a separate matter — the check fails before argument handling is reached.

## This is not a permissions gap, so no allowlist entry fixes it

The command already declares `allowed-tools: Bash(python3:*)` at `:4`, and the instance's `.claude/settings.json` independently allows `Bash(python3:*)`. Neither helps. The checker declines to match *any* rule against a command carrying a simple expansion, rather than failing to find a matching one. The expansions have to leave the `!` line.

Note the contrast that makes this easy to miss: the **same** `$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` expansion is fine in `template/.claude/settings.json:66`, because a `hooks` entry's `command` is executed directly and never routed through the permission checker.

## Why it bites: the only documented remedy is the command that cannot run

Enforcement is unaffected. The Stop hook (`template/.claude/settings.json:60-68`) still blocks a leaf that ends without discharging its contract, and tells it:

> Write the missing/malformed artifact(s), verify with `/handoff <id>` …
> — `template/.claude/hooks/handoff_guard.py:68`

…which is the broken command. The gate holds while its published remedy path is unusable. The way out is to know that the guard's own CLI is the same check:

```
python3 .claude/hooks/handoff_guard.py --check issue_507
handoff(planner) issue_507: PASS — the planner exit contract is discharged
```

That works (verified above, exit 0), but it appears nowhere in what a leaf is told — `handoff_guard.py:18` documents `--check <id>` as the CLI *the rendered command uses*, not as something a leaf invokes itself.

## Scope

- One occurrence. `handoff.md.jinja` is the only file under `template/.claude/commands/`.
- Copied verbatim into every render: the instance's `.claude/commands/handoff.md` is byte-identical to the rendered template (`{{ cli_name }}` is the only substitution in the file, and it is not on line 13).
- Introduced with the command itself in `900d638` ("Add a checked exit contract for the interactive leaves", #331). I have **not** established when the checker's behaviour changed, so I can't say whether this ever worked.

## The fix shape is not obvious — two questions to settle

1. **`$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` looks removable.** Line 19 of the same file already writes the relative form `python3 .claude/hooks/handoff_guard.py` for the abandon hatch, so a relative path is evidently expected to resolve from where a slash command runs. Worth confirming rather than assuming.
2. **`$1` is the harder half.** It is Claude Code's own argument placeholder, not a shell variable — but the error shows the checker seeing it *unsubstituted*, so the ordering of placeholder substitution and permission checking decides whether any argument-passing form survives in a `!` block. If none does, the id has to reach the guard another way: the guard resolving it from session state, or the command dropping the `!` block entirely and instructing the model to make the Bash call itself (which `allowed-tools: Bash(python3:*)` already permits, and which the `--abandon` line at `:19` already implies is an acceptable shape).

## Related

#404 proposes rendering the deliberate-abandon hatch as an `/abandon` slash command instead of a raw hook invocation. Written in the same shape it hits the same wall — settling the question above first would keep that from shipping broken too.
title: /handoff cannot run in any rendered instance — its `!` block carries shell expansions the permission checker refuses
